theme: Judging, asking, the narrow way, the two foundations
readingInstruction: Read Matthew 7:1-29. Jesus ends the Sermon with warnings about judging, a call to ask the Father, the narrow gate, false prophets, and the two builders. Pay attention to the last verses of the chapter.
settingTheScene: The final chapter of the Sermon moves from describing the kingdom life to urging a response. Jesus warns his hearers against false religion and calls for decision. The Sermon ends not with a list of rules but with a choice between two roads, two trees, and two foundations. Everyone who hears must act.
observation: “Judge not, that you be not judged” (7:1).
“First take the log out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to take the speck out of your brother’s eye” (7:5).
“Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you” (7:7).
“So whatever you wish that others would do to you, do also to them, for this is the Law and the Prophets” (7:12).
“Enter by the narrow gate. For the gate is wide and the way is easy that leads to destruction” (7:13).
“You will recognize them by their fruits” (7:16).
“Not everyone who says to me, Lord, Lord, will enter the kingdom of heaven, but the one who does the will of my Father” (7:21).
“And when Jesus finished these sayings, the crowds were astonished at his teaching, for he was teaching them as one who had authority” (7:28-29).
interpretation:
Jesus does not forbid all discernment, since he later tells us to recognize false prophets by their fruit. He forbids a harsh, hypocritical spirit that picks at others’ faults while ignoring our own. The image of a log in the eye is humorous and deliberate. First deal with yourself, and then you can help your brother with clear sight.

The call to ask, seek, and knock comes back again, because the Christian life depends on a Father who gives. And the Golden Rule sums up the whole ethic: treat others as you want to be treated. It is the Law and the Prophets in a sentence.

Then comes a choice. There are two gates, one wide and easy, and one narrow and hard. There are two kinds of trees and two kinds of fruit. The popular road is not the safe one. Jesus’ warning that some who say “Lord, Lord” will be turned away is one of the most sobering in the Bible. These people did religious things, prophesied, cast out demons, and did mighty works in his name. But he says, “I never knew you.” The test is not activity but a relationship with Christ shown in obedience.

The closing story is of two builders. Both heard the same words. One built on rock and one on sand. The storm tested both, and only the house on the rock stood. The difference was not hearing but doing. The crowds were astonished, because Jesus taught with his own authority, not by quoting other rabbis. The one who has given the Sermon is also the one who will judge. The way to be safe is to build on him.
connection: Romans 2:1 warns that when you judge another, you condemn yourself. James 1:22-25 says to be doers of the word and not hearers only. Luke 6:46-49 gives the parallel to the two builders. John 10:9: “I am the door; if anyone enters by me, he will be saved.” John 14:6: “I am the way, and the truth, and the life.” Ephesians 2:20 says Christ Jesus himself is the cornerstone. 1 Corinthians 3:11: no one can lay a foundation other than Christ.
application:
Ask where you are looking at the speck in someone else while ignoring your own log. Confess it.

Pick one thing from the Sermon on the Mount that you have heard but not done. Do it this week.

Ask yourself honestly: are you building your life on Christ, or on something that will not survive a storm?
prayerPrompts: Confess where you judge others while ignoring your own sin.
Ask him to help you enter by the narrow way.
Ask him to build your life on the rock of his words.
